_meta.indication: SOTYKTU is indicated for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Not recommended in combination with other potent immunosuppressants.

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active comparator (apremilast)-controlled trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis; candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy; PASI ≥12, sPGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: proportion achieving sPGA 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.result: sPGA 0/1: 54% vs 7% placebo; PASI 75: 58% vs 13% placebo (p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active comparator (apremilast)-controlled trial with randomized withdrawal/maintenance
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis; candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy; PASI ≥12, sPGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: proportion achieving sPGA 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.result: sPGA 0/1: 50% vs 9% placebo; PASI 75: 53% vs 9% placebo (p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory infections (19.2% vs 14.8% placebo), blood creatine phosphokinase increased (2.7% vs 1.2%), herpes simplex (2.0% vs 0.2%), mouth ulcers (1.9% vs 0.0%), folliculitis (1.7% vs 0.0%), and acne (1.4% vs 0.2%).
target_moa: Deucravacitinib is a selective tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitor. It binds the pseudokinase (regulatory) domain of TYK2, stabilizing an autoinhibitory interaction with the catalytic domain, thereby inhibiting kinase activity and downstream STAT signaling; the exact mechanism in psoriasis is unknown.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; a Medical Policy and Program Review Council (MPPRC) discussion took place July 6, 2022.

description.text: Added indication for the treatment of adults with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the treatment of adults with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA).

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) NDA 214958 for deucravacitinib, a first-in-class new molecular entity oral TYK2 inhibitor, received September 10, 2021 and approved September 9, 2022 on the first review cycle for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis; no advisory committee was convened and no expedited-program designations are documented.

requirement.text: 4336-1 (PREA): Randomized controlled trial of safety, efficacy, and PK of deucravacitinib in adolescents (12 to <18 years) with moderate to severe psoriasis; ≥300 subjects at highest proposed dosage for ≥52 weeks.

citations.quote: Conduct a randomized, controlled trial to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of deucravacitinib in the adolescent population (12 years to less than 18 years) with moderate to severe psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Evaluate at least 300 subjects exposed to deucravacitinib at the highest proposed dosage for a minimum of 52 weeks.

requirement.text: 4336-2 (PREA): Trial of safety, efficacy, and PK of deucravacitinib in pediatric subjects 4 to <12 years with moderate to severe psoriasis; ≥150 subjects at highest proposed dosage for ≥52 weeks.

citations.quote: Conduct a trial to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of deucravacitinib in pediatric subjects 4 years to less than 12 years of age with moderate to severe psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Evaluate at least 150 subjects exposed to deucravacitinib at the highest proposed dosage for a minimum of 52 weeks.

requirement.text: 4336-3 (Pregnancy): Prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to deucravacitinib during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: Conduct a prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to deucravacitinib during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 4336-4 (Pregnancy): Pregnancy study of a different design (e.g., retrospective cohort or case-control) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, and preterm birth in women exposed to deucravacitinib during pregnancy vs unexposed controls.

citations.quote: Conduct a pregnancy study that uses a different design from the pregnancy registry (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to deucravacitinib during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 4336-5 (Lactation): Lactation study (milk only) in lactating women who received deucravacitinib to assess concentrations in breastmilk using a validated assay.

citations.quote: Perform a lactation study (milk only) in lactating women who have received deucravacitinib to assess concentrations of deucravacitinib in breastmilk using a validated assay.

requirement.text: 4336-6 (Long-Term Safety): Randomized, active-controlled clinical trial to evaluate long-term safety of deucravacitinib in patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, characterizing cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.

citations.quote: Conduct a randomized, active-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of deucravacitinib in patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. The trial should be of sufficient size and duration to characterize safety events of interest, including cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.
